2607.04560.title: Can temporal article-level credibility signals improve domain-level credibility prediction?
2607.04560.paper_summary: Web domain credibility evaluation is vital for combating misinformation. It is conducted by examining factors such as domain type, transparency, and overall reputation. However, assessing the credibility of newly emerging web domains remains challenging since they have no reputation yet. Expert fact-checkers evaluate the credibility of domains by analyzing the content of their articles, including the presence of misinformation, bias, or propaganda. Yet, the ease of large-scale content generation enabled by LLMs has accelerated the creation of new content, rendering manual assessment insufficient and underscoring the need for automated approaches to domain credibility evaluation. In this paper, we introduce our Domain Credibility Evaluation Framework (DCEF), a temporal framework for domain credibility evaluation grounded in expert ratings. DCEF enables us to investigate whether the credibility of web domains can be assessed from their published articles following the workflow of expert fact-checkers, without any prior knowledge of the source domains themselves.
2607.04560.paper_summary_zh: 網域可信度評估對於打擊錯誤資訊至關重要。這是通過檢查網域類型、透明度和整體聲譽等因素來進行的。然而，評估新興網域的可信度仍然具有挑戰性，因為它們尚無聲譽。專家事實查核者通過分析文章內容來評估網域的可信度，包括錯誤資訊、偏見或宣傳的存在。然而，LLMs所促進的大規模內容生成的便利性加速了新內容的創建，使得手動評估不足以應對，並強調了自動化網域可信度評估方法的需求。在本文中，我們介紹了我們的網域可信度評估框架（DCEF），這是一個基於專家評級的網域可信度評估的時間框架。DCEF使我們能夠調查網域的可信度是否可以從其發表的文章中進行評估，遵循專家事實查核者的工作流程，而無需對源網域本身有任何先前的了解。
